economic_mechanism: Weekly EIA storage-change surprises (actual minus a documented pre-release consensus) carry information not yet in price because the release is a discrete scheduled news event; markets react to the surprise component, not the level.
prior_evidence: Event study (Linn & Zhu, citation unconfirmed, sample 2002-2011): significant inverse relationship between storage-change surprise and same-day futures/spot price change. Corroborated qualitatively by extensive 2025-2026 trade-press evidence of 3-5% announcement-day moves.
target: Henry Hub / front-month NG next-session (or same-session post-release) log return
candidate_inputs: a fixed, documented pre-release consensus-forecast source
pit_requirements: PIT_READY for the actual (EIA release archive exists); PIT_POSSIBLE_WITH_WORK for the consensus benchmark -- a consistent historical consensus source must be fixed and its own publication timing documented.
baseline_control: Zero-return naive (existing V1 control) plus a storage-day-only dummy to separate day-of-week effects from surprise-magnitude effects.
expected_direction: Larger-than-expected withdrawal (or smaller-than-expected injection) -> positive same/next-session return.
required_interactions: None for the base test; a secondary, separately preregistered test could interact the surprise with current storage-vs-seasonal-norm tightness.
falsification_criterion: No statistically and economically material improvement over the naive baseline on 2016-2026 (current-regime) data, using the same walk-forward/OOS discipline as the frozen V1/V2 contract.
key_risks: Underlying academic evidence predates the shale/LNG-export era and needs replication on current data; a clean PIT-safe consensus-forecast source must be located and verified.
recommended_next_action: Locate and verify a PIT-safe consensus-forecast source for the weekly storage report; replicate the event-study design on 2016-2026 data as the first, cheapest, best horizon-matched test.

economic_mechanism: Short-lead-time weather-forecast revisions move expected near-term heating/cooling demand before it is realised; if the market underreacts to revisions relative to levels, forecast-revision content should be more informative than realised-weather content at short horizons.
prior_evidence: Industry case study (World Climate Service, 2026; NOT peer-reviewed): significant relationship between CONUS HDD-anomaly forecasts and Henry Hub spot-price volatility, strongest at 2-4 day lead, decaying beyond 10-14 days, consistent across GFS/GEFS/ECMWF. No peer-reviewed academic corroboration independently located.
target: Henry Hub next-session return or short-horizon realised volatility
pit_requirements: PIT_POSSIBLE_WITH_WORK -- forecast issuance is naturally PIT-correct by timestamp; archive depth and cost (especially ECMWF) need confirmation.
baseline_control: Naive; a realised-weather-only control to isolate the incremental value of the revision over the level.
expected_direction: A cooling (bullish, winter) or warming (bullish, summer cooling-demand) revision at short lead time -> same-direction price move, decaying with lead time.
required_interactions: Season (winter HDD-driven vs summer CDD-driven) should be modelled as a fixed interaction, not pooled.
falsification_criterion: No material OOS improvement over the realised-weather-only control, or no lead-time decay pattern consistent with the vendor study's claimed profile.
key_risks: No peer-reviewed replication located; possible vendor selection/marketing bias; ECMWF archive cost unconfirmed.
recommended_next_action: Dedicated academic-literature search on weather-forecast-revision (not realised-weather) effects in energy markets; treat as second-priority near-term US-only test.

economic_mechanism: H-GLOBAL-LNG-1 narrowed and re-horizoned: EU storage tightness raises the netback incentive to route flexible LNG cargoes toward Europe; this only translates into a measurable US domestic effect when US liquefaction capacity is actually utilised near its ceiling.
prior_evidence: Mixed. Contemporaneous/explanatory support strong (IEA, ACER, ECB; Farag & Ruhnau 2026; Szafranek et al. 2023 on conditional EU connectedness). Direct US-side transmission evidence weak-to-negative: Rubaszek & Szafranek (2025) find the 2021-2023 European crisis only marginally affected the US market; Farag, Jeddi & Kopp (2025) find the US market DECOUPLED from EU/Asia during the most acute 2021-2022 stress window due to infrastructure congestion.
horizon: Weeks to months, NOT 1 trading session -- no reviewed source demonstrates next-session forecast content from this channel; every peer-reviewed source operates at weekly/monthly/quarterly frequency.
candidate_inputs: US LNG feedgas/export volume and liquefaction utilisation
pit_requirements: PIT_POSSIBLE_WITH_WORK across the board; JKM leg leans UNSUITABLE without a confirmed Platts licence budget.
baseline_control: Frozen US-only comparator per H-GLOBAL-LNG-1's own test ladder A/B/C/D, evaluated at weekly/monthly horizon in addition to (not instead of) the daily target, so a horizon-driven null can be distinguished from a mechanism-driven one.
expected_direction: Higher EU storage deficit x higher US LNG utilisation -> tighter US domestic balance -> higher HH price/volatility.
required_interactions: EU-storage-deficit x US-LNG-utilisation as already specified, PLUS an explicit infrastructure-congestion state variable given the Farag/Jeddi/Kopp decoupling finding, or the interaction term will silently average over a regime where the mechanism inverts.
falsification_criterion: As specified in the existing H-GLOBAL-LNG-1 stop conditions, with the addition that a genuine test must first run at a horizon with actual peer-reviewed support before a 1-session-horizon failure is treated as informative about the mechanism itself.
key_risks: Horizon mismatch; JKM data cost/licensing; the single most on-point paper leans skeptical of aggregate transmission.
recommended_next_action: Do not activate at the current V1/V2 1-session horizon. If pursued, re-scope as a weekly- or monthly-horizon test, run strictly after H2 and H3 have been tested and their results banked.

economic_mechanism: The shape of the futures curve (contango/backwardation, calendar-spread level) reflects storage/seasonal fundamentals and, for the spot-futures spread specifically, has been shown to carry predictive content for the future spot price.
prior_evidence: Demonstrated at 9-24 month horizons for the spot-futures spread (Baumeister, Huber, Lee & Ravazzolo 2024, NBER WP 33156): beats random walk at all evaluated horizons, largest gains 9-15 months. A separate mean-reversion calendar-spread strategy result (Sharpe >2 for natural gas after costs, 1992-2013) was found only at abstract level and is NOT independently verified.
target: Henry Hub level (spread-forecast version) or a calendar-spread return (mean-reversion version -- unverified)
horizon: 9-24 months (verified) vs days-to-weeks (unverified claim) -- two distinct hypotheses that should not be conflated
candidate_inputs: NG futures curve by contract-month settlement prices
pit_requirements: PIT_READY for raw settlement data; continuous/spread series construction must be fixed and documented to avoid roll-artefact contamination.
baseline_control: Naive; also the pure futures-price no-change forecast (both are 'model-free' benchmarks in the source paper's own terminology).
expected_direction: Not directional in a fixed-sign sense -- the spread model's forecast direction is data-determined by the current spread level.
required_interactions: None required for the base 9-24 month test.
falsification_criterion: No OOS improvement over the futures-no-change and random-walk benchmarks on current-regime data.
key_risks: 9-24 month verified horizon is far longer than Commodity's current 1-session target; mean-reversion/calendar-spread version is unverified.
recommended_next_action: Treat the 9-24 month spread-forecast result as a candidate for a separate, longer-horizon experiment track. Independently verify the mean-reversion calendar-spread claim before using it for anything.

economic_mechanism: TTF/JKM price levels or the TTF-JKM spread used directly, without the conditioning interactions in H1, as predictors of Henry Hub.
prior_evidence: Weakest in the portfolio. Loureiro, Inchauspe & Aguilera (2023) explicitly reject a simple price-levelling/arbitrage read of LNG-flow data; no reviewed source demonstrates OOS forecast content from raw global price levels for Henry Hub specifically.
target: Henry Hub -- same horizon ambiguity as H1
baseline_control: Frozen US-only comparator (matches H-GLOBAL-LNG-1's own ladder step B).
expected_direction: Not well-specified without conditioning variables -- this is precisely the weakness of this version.
required_interactions: None -- that is the point of this version and also its weakness.
key_risks: Most likely to produce a spurious-correlation-driven false positive precisely because it lacks the conditioning that makes the mechanism economically coherent.
recommended_next_action: Retain only as the required baseline comparator inside the H1 test ladder; do not test as a standalone hypothesis.

economic_mechanism: Use observable state variables (LNG-terminal outage status, EU storage-vs-norm extremity, Strait-of-Hormuz-type disruption flags) to flag periods of elevated volatility/regime change, informing risk sizing and model-selection rather than direction.
prior_evidence: Strong explanatory support that natural-gas forecasting is genuinely regime-dependent: Baumeister et al. (2024) document the best-performing model class itself changes across four historical regimes; Farag & Ruhnau (2026) and Szafranek et al. (2023) document sharp, event-driven connectedness collapses and rebounds; the live 2026 Strait-of-Hormuz/Qatar episode is a real-time illustration.
target: Realised volatility / regime indicator, not the price-return target itself
pit_requirements: Weakest in the portfolio for the outage/event component (no confirmed systematic PIT feed); stronger for the storage-based component.
required_interactions: By construction, this IS the interaction layer for H1, H2 and H3 rather than a competing standalone signal.
falsification_criterion: No improvement in conditional-coverage/volatility-forecast accuracy, or no improvement in H1-H4 OOS performance when the regime flag is added as a conditioning variable.
key_risks: A systematic, PIT-archived outage/event feed does not appear to exist off-the-shelf; building one is a data-engineering project, not a data-acquisition task.
recommended_next_action: Lowest near-term priority as a standalone build; revisit as an enhancement to H1's interaction design once H2/H3 have established whether the underlying return-forecasting layer works at all.
